method_notes: Completed means an intact final report, successful exit, no application-budget stop and requested duration within one second; it is not a capacity or protocol-success guarantee.
All rates are per individual run; run labels are manually assigned and unknown sources are never assumed to be the same build.
NIC deltas cover all traffic on the S1 egress interface during the sampled interval, including SSH and unrelated traffic; loopback packets are not included.
CPU and memory peaks are sampled values. Tracker CPU is in cores; host CPU is percent of total available CPU time.
Internal latency buckets include the server-covered HTTP/UDP operations and are not success-only or end-to-end. The final open-ended bucket has null upper bound.
Maintenance maximum is a lifetime high-water. A run maximum is known only when it exceeds the pre-run high-water; unchanged does not mean zero.
OOM and restart increments are observed lower bounds; counter resets can hide intervening events.
A pressure run does not independently verify the network path or dual-stack peer discovery; consult a separate verification result.
Manual diagnostic labels are externally confirmed annotations, not error details recovered from the sanitized runner report.
Before-phase data may be absent in legacy reports; those sample deltas are lower-bound windows rather than complete run totals.
UDP socket queues are sampled bytes; TCP listening queues are sampled connection counts and their configured limits, summed over matching IPv4/IPv6 listeners. Uncollected gauges remain null.

A true decoder_allows_private_test marks a controlled legacy run with the public-address reply filter relaxed; it does not establish a public-only reply assertion. Independent exact-endpoint verification remains separate.
